issues.legal_issue: An executing court cannot entertain a challenge to a decree’s jurisdiction when deciding the challenge requires inquiry into facts not apparent on the face of the record.
material_facts: The decree for ejectment had been affirmed on appeal and in further proceedings, and the jurisdictional objection was first raised when execution was sought.
The alleged lack of jurisdiction depended on interpreting the lease and determining the use of the land, matters requiring examination beyond the face of the record.
issues.conclusion: The executing court could not investigate those facts to decide whether the decree was without jurisdiction, and the jurisdictional objection had to be rejected in execution.
issues.legal_principle: An executing court must take a decree according to its tenor and cannot go behind it; an erroneous decree remains binding until set aside in an appropriate proceeding. A decree that is a nullity, or that was made by a court lacking inherent jurisdiction, may be challenged in execution when the defect appears on the face of the record. If deciding the objection requires examining matters raised or capable of being raised at trial, the executing court cannot entertain it. The Court referred to Jnanendra Mohan Bhaduri v. Rabindra Nath Chakravarti for a jurisdictional defect apparent on the record. It also explained that sections 5(8) and 6 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, made the court’s jurisdiction depend on the premises and their use; Mst. Subhadra v. Narasaji Chenaji Marwadi was cited concerning the date for determining agricultural use. The Court noted the distinction for objections apparent on the record, subject to the stated exceptions concerning territorial jurisdiction and section 11 of the Suits Valuation Act.

rule.if: execution_proceeding and jurisdiction_objection_requires_fact_inquiry and not jurisdictional_defect_apparent_on_record and decree_not_set_aside

predicates.execution_proceeding: A party is asking a court to enforce an existing decree.
predicates.jurisdiction_objection_requires_fact_inq: The party's claim that the decree was made without jurisdiction can be resolved only by examining facts or matters beyond the face of the record.
predicates.jurisdictional_defect_apparent_on_record: The alleged jurisdictional defect is evident from the face of the record.
predicates.decree_not_set_aside: The decree has not been set aside in an appropriate proceeding.

issues.definition: When enforcement of an unset-aside decree is sought and the alleged jurisdictional defect is not apparent from the record but requires factual inquiry, the executing court must reject the jurisdictional objection.
